speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you've been experiencing headaches and worsening vision for three weeks. To better understand your condition, can you describe the specific location and type of pain you feel in your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Is the headache located on one side of your head, does it throb or feel like pressure, and does it improve with rest or worsen with exertion? Also, have you noticed any sudden flashes of light, new blind spots, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with Contrast. REQUEST IMAGES. While I review those, can you tell me if your vision loss is gradual in one eye or both, or if it fluctuates throughout the day?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Visual_Acuity: Right_Eye 20/120, Left_Eye 20/80; Fundoscopy: Findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)
